topic.SIMON.ambient 2.002: Then we’ll give it a guard.
topic.SIMON.ambient 2.x01: And the cart a detour. People will have to push it the long way round.
topic.SIMON.ambient 2.x02: Will whoever pushes it like that?
topic.SIMON.ambient 2.x03: No. But in ten years he’ll sit down in the shade and forget.
topic.SIMON.extra 1.label: Trees on the estate
topic.SIMON.extra 1.001: How many trees will there be here once the estate is finished?
topic.SIMON.extra 1.002: As many as we plant and as many as survive their first three winters.
topic.SIMON.extra 1.004: More, when nobody runs them over with a cart. That’s why I worry so much about that lime.
topic.SIMON.extra 1.006: After that they defend themselves. A tree with thick bark only fears saws and people with plans.
topic.SIMON.extra 2.label: The school garden
topic.SIMON.extra 2.001: What do you grow in the school garden?
topic.SIMON.extra 2.002: Carrots, beans and peas. The children sow them in spring and are amazed in September that something has grown.
topic.SIMON.extra 2.004: Now we’re planning what to sow in spring. And the children are already arguing about who gets to do the watering.
topic.SKLAD.ambient 1.label: Have you got everything?
topic.SKLAD.ambient 1.001: Not everything. But I know exactly what we haven’t got.
topic.SKLAD.ambient 1.x01: Brass round-head screws, blue paint, and one spanner somebody borrowed in fifty-eight.
topic.SKLAD.ambient 1.x02: And are you looking for that spanner?
topic.SKLAD.ambient 1.x03: No. I know exactly where it is. That person just doesn’t know yet that I know.
topic.SKLAD.ambient 2.label: What do you want those offcuts for?
topic.SKLAD.ambient 2.001: Without small pieces, a big thing often won’t budge.
topic.SKLAD.ambient 2.002: And what can you make from a piece like that?
topic.SKLAD.ambient 2.x01: A washer, a seal, a loop. With one offcut I once mended an entire stable door.
topic.SKLAD.ambient 2.x03: The hinge. But without a hinge a door is just a plank, so – entire.
topic.SKLAD.extra 1.label: Oto’s slips
topic.SKLAD.extra 1.001: Does Mr Bielik write slips often?
topic.SKLAD.extra 1.002: Every week. Neatly, with measurements and a signature. It’s a pleasure to issue materials against a slip like that.
topic.SKLAD.extra 1.003: And which slips don’t you like?
topic.SKLAD.extra 1.004: The ones that say ‘something for repairs’. We don’t stock an item called ‘something’. Nobody has that.
topic.SKLAD.extra 2.label: Children in the yard
topic.SKLAD.extra 2.001: Why aren’t children allowed in here?
topic.SKLAD.extra 2.002: Because everything here is sharp, heavy or on record. Children would mix it all up.
topic.SKLAD.extra 2.003: A little girl once counted my sacks over the fence. I had two more than I thought.
topic.SKLAD.extra 2.005: Not for a store. I thought I knew exactly what we had.
topic.TONO82.ambient 1.label: What are you making?
topic.TONO82.ambient 1.001: A swallow. Grandad says even a model has to have the right centre of gravity.
topic.TONO82.ambient 1.002: So does a person. It’s just harder to measure.
topic.TONO82.ambient 1.003: Then we’ll make him a stand.
topic.TONO82.ambient 1.x01: And where will the swallow live?
topic.TONO82.ambient 1.x02: On the window next to Grandad. You can see the whole yard from there.
topic.TONO82.ambient 2.label: Do you like school?
topic.TONO82.ambient 2.001: In the prep room, yes. There every thing does what it’s for.
topic.TONO82.ambient 2.003: Elsewhere you have to say everything with the right words first.
topic.TONO82.ambient 2.x01: In lessons you mustn’t say ‘that thing’. You have to say ‘component’ or ‘teaching aid’.
topic.TONO82.ambient 2.x02: And what’s that you’re holding called?
topic.TONO82.ambient 2.x03: At home, a wing. At school, technical model, part one.
topic.TONO82.extra 1.label: St Nicholas
topic.TONO82.extra 1.001: Did St Nicholas come to your house yesterday?
topic.TONO82.extra 1.002: He did. He brought me chocolate and coal. Grandad says the coal is for the alarm clock I took apart.
topic.TONO82.extra 1.003: You took an alarm clock apart?
topic.TONO82.extra 1.004: I did. And put it back together. I just had one part left over.
topic.TONO82.extra 1.005: That happens to the best of us.
topic.TONO82.extra 1.006: Grandad says not to the best. But it probably happens to you too, doesn’t it?
topic.TONO82.extra 2.label: When you grow up
topic.TONO82.extra 2.001: What do you want to be when you grow up?
topic.TONO82.extra 2.002: An aircraft designer. Or a pilot. Anything but a caretaker.
topic.TONO82.extra 2.004: A caretaker has to carry a hundred keys and know which one’s for what. That would bore me.
topic.TONO82.extra 2.005: Hm. Keys can be quite interesting.
topic.TONO82.extra 2.006: You sound like Grandad. He says every door has its own trick too.
topic.TONO82.extra 3.label: Swallows
topic.TONO82.extra 3.001: Why do you draw swallows everywhere?
topic.TONO82.extra 3.002: Because they come back. Every spring to the same place, even though they fly across the whole sea.
topic.TONO82.extra 3.004: I haven’t been anywhere yet. But if I had, I definitely would.
topic.VERA60.ambient 1.label: Why do you draw outdoors?
topic.VERA60.ambient 1.001: For the light. And out here Oto can’t change the measurements on me every three minutes.
topic.VERA60.ambient 1.002: I know that kind of customer too – the one who keeps changing the brief.
topic.VERA60.ambient 1.x01: And what do you do with him?
topic.VERA60.ambient 1.x02: I write down the first brief. When he comes back, I show him where he started.
topic.VERA60.ambient 1.x03: I’ll try that on Oto. Though he’ll only show me what my first drawing looked like.
topic.VERA60.ambient 2.label: What is an accurate drawing?
topic.VERA60.ambient 2.001: One where the next person doesn’t have to guess what we meant.
topic.VERA60.ambient 2.002: You should write instructions for household appliances.
topic.VERA60.ambient 2.x01: Does anyone read those? I thought they were included so there’d be something to lose.
topic.VERA60.ambient 2.x02: In my workshop they’re the first thing to go missing.
topic.VERA60.extra 1.label: The girl playing hopscotch
topic.VERA60.extra 1.001: That little girl playing hopscotch – does she keep you company here every day?
topic.VERA60.extra 1.002: Zuzka? Every day. She hops, she counts, and now and then she tells me one of my lines is crooked.
topic.VERA60.extra 1.004: It is. That’s why I’d rather keep her counting, so she doesn’t check my lines.
topic.VERA60.extra 3.label: What are you drawing now?
topic.VERA60.extra 3.001: What have you got on your drawing board?
topic.VERA60.extra 3.002: A cross-section of ZVON. So that one day even someone who wasn’t there can repair it.
topic.VERA60.extra 3.004: For example. Though you look as if you’ve been near it already.
topic.VERA60.extra 2.label: Your drawings
topic.VERA60.extra 2.001: Are you drawing that for Mr Bielik?
topic.VERA60.extra 2.002: For Oto. This morning he told me it was finished. At lunchtime, nearly finished. Now it’s a draft.
topic.VERA60.extra 2.003: And what do you do about that?
topic.VERA60.extra 2.004: I draw in pencil. I’m saving the ink for the day Oto stops changing the measurements.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 1.label: Who are you?
topic.ZUZANA.extra 1.002: I am. But I don’t go to nursery any more. I’m in the first year at school.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 1.003: Twenty-four more days and I’ll have done the whole first year.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 1.005: I count everything. Squares, stairs, and how many times Uncle Rudo forgets his lines.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 1.006: And how many times has he forgotten them today?
topic.ZUZANA.extra 1.007: Eleven times so far. But it isn’t evening yet.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 1.009: I’m Zuzana. You’re not from here. You talk differently.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 1.011: Like the radio from Bratislava. Nicely, but fast.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 2.label: Oto’s workshop
topic.ZUZANA.extra 2.001: Do you know where Mr Bielik has his workshop?
topic.ZUZANA.extra 2.002: Uncle Oto? You can find him by the sound.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 2.003: From the green, go where it smells of leather. That’s the yard, and Uncle Štefan is there.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 2.004: And past him, go where it ticks from every side. That’s Uncle Oto.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 2.005: The smell of leather, then the ticking. I’ll remember that.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 2.006: Just don’t go where it clucks. That’s only the hens.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 3.label: Mrs Lída
topic.ZUZANA.extra 3.001: Do you know where I can find Mrs Lída from the theatre?
topic.ZUZANA.extra 3.002: Auntie Lída is in the hall. Where someone is shouting ‘Never fear, darling!’
topic.ZUZANA.extra 3.003: Their fabric forest wobbles all day long. One screw is loose – I saw it.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 3.005: I did. But nobody will lend me a screwdriver, because I’m little.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 3.006: I’ve got one in my bag.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 3.007: They probably won’t take yours away. You’re big.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 4.label: The pump by the hut
topic.ZUZANA.extra 4.001: That pump by the hut behind the park…
topic.ZUZANA.extra 4.002: It drips. This morning I counted a hundred drips, then I stopped.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 4.004: Because after a hundred there was nothing interesting. Just more drips.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 4.005: Auntie Mira says the pump needs a new cuff.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 4.006: I thought a cuff was on a shirt. A pump hasn’t got a shirt.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 4.007: This one’s made of leather. It keeps the water where it’s supposed to be.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 4.008: So it’s a sort of belt for water.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 5.002: Auntie Mira from the hut? All of Ivanka knows her.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 5.003: When the hut by the channel has its light on in the daytime, the grown-ups say: ‘Mira’s measuring time again.’
topic.ZUZANA.extra 5.004: And do you know what that means?
topic.ZUZANA.extra 5.005: No. But she does it very precisely. Once she timed how long it takes me to do the hopscotch.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 5.007: Twenty-two seconds. Now it’s twenty-one. I’m practising.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 6.label: The pigeon by the bowl
topic.ZUZANA.extra 6.001: Is that pigeon by the bowl your friend?
topic.ZUZANA.extra 6.002: No, he’s Mr Baran’s. He’s a carrier pigeon – he’s got a ring on his leg.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 6.003: I gave him some bread, but he didn’t want it. He must be used to better.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 6.004: Maybe he wants his own feed.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 6.005: Uncle Štefan in the yard will have that. He has everything you can pour.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 6.006: And don’t chase him. When someone chases him, he flies exactly where you don’t want him to.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 8.001: What are you going to do in the holidays?
topic.ZUZANA.extra 8.002: I’m going to go to the channel and watch the water flow. We’re not allowed in the water, only to watch.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 8.003: And I’m going to go to the station. Uncle Božo lets me wave to the trains to Bratislava.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 8.005: Only the ones that are on time. He waves to the others himself. Crossly.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 7.label: The play
topic.ZUZANA.extra 7.001: Do they put on plays here too?
topic.ZUZANA.extra 7.002: They do. Uncle Rudo is rehearsing in the hall, and I already know his first line: ‘Never fear, darling!’
topic.ZUZANA.extra 7.004: Not even he knows the second. It’s in the script, and the script got lost.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 7.005: Auntie Lída says if it isn’t found, it’ll be a very short play.
topic.ZUZANA.extra 7.007: I’d clap. But only a little, so he doesn’t think that’s enough.
item.SUPPLYSLIP: Oto’s slip for Štefan: one pre-cut leather cuff and two hollow rivets.
item.SUPPLYSLIP.purpose: Collect the leather and rivets from Štefan.
item.LEATHER: The leather is cut to size. Two marked holes still need punching.
item.LEATHER.purpose: Make a new cuff for the hand pump.
item.RIVETS: Two hollow rivets. They’ll join the cuff into a ring.
item.PUNCH: A punch and pliers in one. Oto will return it to Lída after the job.
item.PUNCH.purpose: Punch the holes in the leather cuff.
item.CUFF_OPEN: The holes are punched. Now I just need to join it with the rivets.
item.CUFF: A new leather cuff. It fits the hand pump’s piston exactly.
item.CUFF.purpose: Fit it to the hand pump so the water circulates again.
item.PUMPKEY: Oto’s key to the measuring room. I got it for mending the pump.
item.PUMPKEY.purpose: Unlock the measuring room door by the pump.
item.REGFORM: Mira’s signed form with today’s date and the measurement results. I need a duplicate and a post office stamp.
item.REGFORM.purpose: Have the post office confirm that the document existed in 1962.
item.STYLUS: Vera’s blunt stylus. It traces the edges of the imprint without scratching the plate.
item.STYLUS.purpose: Finish a legible imprint without damaging the plate.
item.WAXPAPER: A soft waxed sheet. An imprint without a camera, the old-fashioned way.
item.WAXPAPER.purpose: Press it onto the calibration plate.
item.PRESSED: The plate’s relief is on the paper, but it’s faint. The edges need tracing with a blunt stylus.
item.PRESSED.purpose: Trace the imprint with the stylus to make it legible.
item.ORIGIN_RAW: Four words, the rule, and Mira’s and Oto’s signatures. The post office confirmation is still missing.
item.ORIGIN_RAW.purpose: Store it with the stamped registration form in the metal box.
item.CARBON: Carbon paper from the post office. I put it between two sheets and one writing gives me two identical copies.
item.CARBON.purpose: The second copy of the registration form.
item.REGDOUBLE: Two identical forms, both signed by Mira. Now just the stamp.
item.REGDOUBLE.purpose: Have Alojz at the post office confirm the date.
item.REGISTERED: A stamp and the number Z-17. The post office has confirmed that the form existed today – not that the physics is right.
item.REGISTERED.purpose: Store it with the copy in the metal box.
item.ORIGIN: The imprint with its storage number. The plate and the archive copy stayed in 1962; I’m carrying this one.
item.ORIGIN.purpose: Proof of origin for the final restore.
item.PARTSNOTE: A requisition slip for a ceramic base and three copper links. Signed by Oto, not by Tóno.
item.PARTSNOTE.purpose: Collect the bridge parts from Marta at the store.
item.CERAMICPARTS: A ceramic base and three marked copper links. Nothing that will leak or rust over the years.
item.CERAMICPARTS.purpose: Assemble the bridge on the service board in the prep room.
item.BRIDGE_NEW: A ceramic bridge built to Oto’s drawing, with no battery, and Tóno’s swallow on the label. I’ll hide it in a dry jar.
item.BRIDGE_NEW.purpose: Store it in a dry, airtight jar.
item.JAR: A dry jar with a rubber seal, and wrapping paper. Oto will add the dried packing.
item.JAR.purpose: Keep the bridge dry in the cavity for 38 years.
item.SEALED_NEW: The jar is sealed and Oto has checked the lid. It belongs in the dry cavity in the low wall, not in the ground.
item.SEALED_NEW.purpose: Hide it in the service cavity so it lasts from 1982 to 2020.
item.TREEGUARD: Three ready-made sections of a tree guard. Šimon agrees to the cart’s new route too.
item.TREEGUARD.purpose: Put it up round the young lime.
item.CACHEMAP: Tóno’s childish but accurate sketch, approved by Oto. Second row from the top, third stone from the left. A little swallow instead of a signature.
item.CACHEMAP.purpose: Find the same hiding place in the yard in 2020.
item.SEEDS: A handful of Béla’s mix from Štefan. Enough for one feed.
item.SEEDS.purpose: Put it in the bowl in the park.
item.PLAY: Rudo’s script, ‘Never Fear, Darling!’ The margins are full of notes.
item.PLAY.purpose: Give it back to Rudo in the village hall.
item.JANA_DRAWING: Jana’s schematic with her notes. It explains why the wiring doesn’t cut off the weak signal.
item.JANA_DRAWING.purpose: With Jana’s agreement, show it to her teacher.
item.JANA_APPROVED: Approval for the exhibition is written on the schematic. Jana’s explanation convinced the teacher.
item.JANA_APPROVED.purpose: Give it back to Jana so she can show her own design.
item.BELL_MUTE: A brass hand bell with a wooden handle. The clapper is wrapped in Zuzana’s hanky; the loop is torn.
item.BELL_MUTE.purpose: Hang the clapper on a new leather loop.
item.ZUZA_SLIP: In printed capitals: SLIP. PLEASE MAY I HAVE ONE BIT OF LEATHER FOR THE BELL. ZUZANA, FIRST YEAR. A little flower in the corner.
item.ZUZA_SLIP.purpose: Hand it to Štefan in the workshop yard.
item.STRAP: A narrow strip of leather from Štefan’s offcuts. Just right for a loop, not a bit more.
item.STRAP.purpose: Hang the bell’s clapper on it.
item.BELL_FIXED: The clapper hangs on the new loop, with the knot hidden inside. It rings clearly, but the first proper ringing belongs to Zuzana.
item.BELL_FIXED.purpose: Give it back to Zuzana in the park.
quest.M08.goal: Find Oto in Ivanka and, with his help, get into the measuring room.
quest.M08.hint.1: Go to Oto’s mechanical workshop in Ivanka. He’ll tell you what needs doing before he lets you near the measurement.
quest.M08.hint.2: With Oto’s slip, collect the leather and rivets from Štefan. Lída in the hall will lend you a punch once you tighten the stage flat clamp for her.
quest.M08.hint.3: Chronometer on Oto → Oto’s requisition slip on Štefan → tool bag on the stage flat clamp in the hall → punch + leather → rivets + punched cuff → finished cuff on the hand pump → talk to Oto → key on the measuring room door.
quest.M09.goal: Talk to young Mira by the device and make a legible imprint, leaving the original where it is.
quest.M09.hint.1: Talk to young Mira in the room of the first ZVON.
quest.M09.hint.2: You’ll find waxed paper in the loft, and Vera in the park will lend you a blunt stylus.
quest.M09.hint.3: Talk to Mira in the room of the first ZVON → blunt stylus from Vera in the manor house park → waxed sheet from the loft → sheet on the calibration plate → blunt stylus + faint imprint.
quest.M10.goal: Have the registration form confirmed at the post office and store it in the metal box as proof of origin.
quest.M10.hint.1: The post office will confirm that the registration form really existed in 1962.
quest.M10.hint.2: The registration form is needed in duplicate. You’ll find carbon paper by the counter at the post office.
quest.M10.hint.3: Carbon paper by the counter → carbon paper + technical registration form → form in duplicate on Alojz → stamped registration form on the metal archive box in the loft; you must have the legible imprint with you.
quest.M11B.goal: In 1982, tell Tóno the truth, hide a spare bridge with him, and notice what in the yard needs protecting.
quest.M11B.hint.1: Tóno and his grandad are at the service window. You have to prove to them where you come from.
quest.M11B.hint.2: Show Tóno the protected photo of the 2020 yard. Then get the bridge parts, a dry jar and a guard for the lime.
quest.M11B.hint.3: Chronometer on Tóno → photo of the 2020 yard on Tóno → Oto’s slip on Marta at the store → parts on the service board in the prep room → jar from Ružena at the shop → jar + new bridge → tree guard from Šimon in the shed → sealed jar on the cavity in the low wall → guard on the lime → Šimon again.
quest.Q6.goal: Help Alojz’s pigeon Béla get back to the post office.
quest.Q6.hint.1: Ask Alojz at the post office where his pigeon Béla is.
quest.Q6.hint.2: Štefan in the workshop yard has Béla’s feed; the bowl is in the manor house park.
quest.Q6.hint.3: Talk to Alojz at the post office → talk to Štefan in the workshop yard → handful of seed in the bowl by the pigeon in the park → Alojz again.
quest.Q6.reward: A print of an old post office stamp as a keepsake, in the album.
quest.Q7.goal: Find Rudo’s lost script and give it back to him before the rehearsal.
quest.Q7.hint.1: Talk to Rudo in the village hall. He lent his script to Mira.
quest.Q7.hint.2: The script is in the technical archive loft, which you reach from the measuring room.
quest.Q7.hint.3: Talk to Rudo in the village hall → Rudo’s script in the technical archive loft → script on Rudo.
quest.Q7.reward: Rudo’s first line and a little programme of the performance in the album.
quest.Q9.goal: Help Jana show her own design, and see what it changes later in her life.
quest.Q9.hint.1: Jana, in the classroom before the exhibition in 1982, is hiding her schematic under the template.
quest.Q9.hint.2: With Jana’s agreement, show her schematic to Mr Dobrovič, her teacher. It’s her idea, not yours.
quest.Q9.hint.3: Talk to Jana in the classroom before the exhibition → Jana’s original schematic on Dobrovič → approved schematic on Jana. If you like, find Jana afterwards in the physics prep room in 1995 and 2020, and in the exhibition room in 2035.
quest.Q9.reward: Jana’s schematic in the album, the club in 1995, laptops for children in 2020 and an exhibition at Grand Jasná in 2035.
quest.Q10.goal: Mend Zuzana’s class bell so she can ring it at the end of the year.
quest.Q10.hint.1: Zuzana, in the manor house park, has a bell that won’t ring.
quest.Q10.hint.2: The bell’s clapper has to hang on a new leather loop. Štefan in the workshop yard has the leather, and Zuzana has already written him a slip.
quest.Q10.hint.3: Talk to Zuzana in the park about the bell → Zuzana’s slip on Štefan → leather offcut + class bell → mended bell on Zuzana.
quest.Q10.reward: Zuzana with her bell, and her chalk hopscotch, in the album.
